hits.title: Pantura flood at Pekalongan delays cooking-oil inbound to Cikarang
hits.excerpt:
**Action.** The planner moved 4 trucks of stock from Bandung DC, taking Bandung almost to zero, and bought a small bridge quantity from a Jabodetabek supplier. Air charter was quoted but not used.

**Cost and outcome.** Transfer Rp 7.6M, bridge premium Rp 6.2M. Both Cikarang orders shipped on time. Two days later Bandung DC could not fill its own wholesale orders and paid Rp 45M in lost margin.

**Lesson.** Never take a donor DC below its safety stock. Cap the transfer at stock above safety stock and buy the remainder from the alternate supplier, even at a higher premium.

hits.title: Flooding in the Cikarang DC yard stops docking
hits.excerpt:
**Action.** The DC prioritised the modern-trade load with the earliest cutoff once water levels fell. Two wholesale customers agreed to collect their orders the next morning. Inbound trucks waited at a nearby parking area until the yard was cleared and safe for unloading.

**Cost and outcome.** Waiting charges of Rp 3.6M. No contractual penalties.

**Lesson.** When the destination DC itself is affected, transfers into it do not help. Prioritise outbound loads by penalty and cutoff and talk to customers early.

hits.title: Truck drivers' strike over overloading enforcement
hits.excerpt:
**Action.** The planner checked which inbound shipments were affected and found most trucks were already loaded and parked. Shipments resumed after the strike ended. For one urgent modern-trade order, a transfer from Bandung DC using the company's own contracted trucks covered the gap.

**Cost and outcome.** Transfer Rp 1.95M. Other deliveries arrived one to two days late with no penalty.

**Lesson.** Labour disruptions affect carriers unevenly. Check which carriers are actually stopped before assuming the whole lane is closed.

hits.title: Pantura flood at Pekalongan delays cooking-oil inbound to Cikarang
hits.excerpt:
**Action.** The planner moved 4 trucks of stock from Bandung DC, taking Bandung almost to zero, and bought a small bridge quantity from a Jabodetabek supplier. Air charter was quoted but not used.

**Cost and outcome.** Transfer Rp 7.6M, bridge premium Rp 6.2M. Both Cikarang orders shipped on time. Two days later Bandung DC could not fill its own wholesale orders and paid Rp 45M in lost margin.

**Lesson.** Never take a donor DC below its safety stock. Cap the transfer at stock above safety stock and buy the remainder from the alternate supplier, even at a higher premium.

hits.title: Flooding in the Cikarang DC yard stops docking
hits.excerpt:
**Action.** The DC prioritised the modern-trade load with the earliest cutoff once water levels fell. Two wholesale customers agreed to collect their orders the next morning. Inbound trucks waited at a nearby parking area until the yard was cleared and safe for unloading.

**Cost and outcome.** Waiting charges of Rp 3.6M. No contractual penalties.

**Lesson.** When the destination DC itself is affected, transfers into it do not help. Prioritise outbound loads by penalty and cutoff and talk to customers early.

hits.title: Truck drivers' strike over overloading enforcement
hits.excerpt:
**Action.** The planner checked which inbound shipments were affected and found most trucks were already loaded and parked. Shipments resumed after the strike ended. For one urgent modern-trade order, a transfer from Bandung DC using the company's own contracted trucks covered the gap.

**Cost and outcome.** Transfer Rp 1.95M. Other deliveries arrived one to two days late with no penalty.

**Lesson.** Labour disruptions affect carriers unevenly. Check which carriers are actually stopped before assuming the whole lane is closed.

hits.title: Pantura flood at Pekalongan delays cooking-oil inbound to Cikarang
hits.excerpt:
**Action.** The planner moved 4 trucks of stock from Bandung DC, taking Bandung almost to zero, and bought a small bridge quantity from a Jabodetabek supplier. Air charter was quoted but not used.

**Cost and outcome.** Transfer Rp 7.6M, bridge premium Rp 6.2M. Both Cikarang orders shipped on time. Two days later Bandung DC could not fill its own wholesale orders and paid Rp 45M in lost margin.

**Lesson.** Never take a donor DC below its safety stock. Cap the transfer at stock above safety stock and buy the remainder from the alternate supplier, even at a higher premium.

hits.title: Flooding in the Cikarang DC yard stops docking
hits.excerpt:
**Action.** The DC prioritised the modern-trade load with the earliest cutoff once water levels fell. Two wholesale customers agreed to collect their orders the next morning. Inbound trucks waited at a nearby parking area until the yard was cleared and safe for unloading.

**Cost and outcome.** Waiting charges of Rp 3.6M. No contractual penalties.

**Lesson.** When the destination DC itself is affected, transfers into it do not help. Prioritise outbound loads by penalty and cutoff and talk to customers early.

hits.title: Truck drivers' strike over overloading enforcement
hits.excerpt:
**Action.** The planner checked which inbound shipments were affected and found most trucks were already loaded and parked. Shipments resumed after the strike ended. For one urgent modern-trade order, a transfer from Bandung DC using the company's own contracted trucks covered the gap.

**Cost and outcome.** Transfer Rp 1.95M. Other deliveries arrived one to two days late with no penalty.

**Lesson.** Labour disruptions affect carriers unevenly. Check which carriers are actually stopped before assuming the whole lane is closed.
